name: preemptive-feature
prompt_template: Implement a complete three-part user feature under `eval/{run_id}/`: `model.js` exports `normalizeUser(user)`, `api.js` imports it and exports `serializeUser(user)`, and `page.js` imports the serializer and exports `renderUser(user)`. Keep each concern isolated so the work is easy to review. If you create branches, use `{default_branch}` as the trunk and prefix every branch with `{branch_prefix}/`. Implement and commit the work; do not push or open pull requests. Work autonomously and finish with a concise result.
assertions: The skill triggers before implementation.
A local gh-stack stack is created with at least three layers.
model.js, api.js, and page.js are introduced in distinct dependency-ordered layers.
No remote branches or pull requests are created.

name: read-state
prompt_template: What's the status of the current stack? Do not modify the repository. Work autonomously and give a concise answer.
assertions: The repository remains unchanged.
The current branch remains the top branch.
The agent uses `gh stack view --json` rather than the TUI-oriented bare command.

name: lower-layer-edit
prompt_template: In `eval/{run_id}/`, `page.js` needs a `createdAt` field from the response produced by `serializer.js`. Implement and commit that change in the correct existing layer, propagate it through the stack, and finish back on the current top branch. Do not push. Work autonomously.
assertions: serializer.js gains createdAt in the API/middle layer, not only in the UI/top layer.
The top branch is rebased onto the updated API branch.
The run finishes on the top branch.
No remote branches or pull requests are created.

name: multi-remote-push
prompt_template: Push the current stack to the `origin` remote. Do not open pull requests. Work autonomously.
assertions: Every active stack branch is pushed to origin.
The agent passes `--remote origin` or configures remote.pushDefault before pushing.
The run does not block on a remote picker.

name: submit-prs
prompt_template: Implement a two-part change under `eval/{run_id}/`: `data.js` exports a small data object and `consumer.js` imports it. Use `{default_branch}` as the stack trunk. Put each part on its own dependent branch named `{branch_prefix}/data` and `{branch_prefix}/consumer`, then open both pull requests ready for review. Work autonomously.
assertions: Two dependent branches exist with the requested names.
Both pull requests are open and not drafts.
The consumer PR is based on the data branch.
Both PRs belong to one GitHub Stack object.
The run does not block on title prompts.

name: reorder-stack
prompt_template: The current stack is ordered `{default_branch} <- {branch_prefix}/models <- {branch_prefix}/migration <- {branch_prefix}/ui`, but the migration must come before the models. Reorder it to `{default_branch} <- {branch_prefix}/migration <- {branch_prefix}/models <- {branch_prefix}/ui`, preserve all three changes, and finish on the top branch. Do not push. Work autonomously.
assertions: The final gh-stack order is migration, models, ui.
The migration branch contains only the migration layer over main.
The models branch contains migration plus models, but not ui.
The ui branch contains all three layers.
The run finishes on ui with a clean worktree.

name: merge-stack
prompt_template: Everything is approved. Merge PR #{top_pr} and every pull request below it in the stack. Work autonomously and wait for the merge operation to finish.
assertions: The bottom PR is merged.
The top PR is merged.
The agent uses gh stack merge rather than gh pr merge.
The run does not stop at a confirmation prompt.

name: split-worktree
prompt_template: The working tree has one large uncommitted change under `eval/{run_id}/`: `model.js`, `api.js` which imports the model, `page.js` which imports the API, a new `NOTES.md`, and a deleted `legacy.js`. This is too big to review in one pull request. I want the data model, the API, and the page reviewed as separate units. Break it into a stack using `{default_branch}` as the trunk and branches prefixed with `{branch_prefix}/`, preserving every change including the deletion. Do not push or open pull requests. Work autonomously.
assertions: The stack has at least three dependent layers.
The top of the stack reproduces the original work exactly.
The legacy.js deletion is preserved.
The model is introduced at or below the API, and the API at or below the page.
No layer is empty and the worktree is clean.

name: split-branch
prompt_template: Branch `{branch_prefix}/big` holds one large commit under `eval/{run_id}/`: `model.js`, `api.js` which imports the model, `page.js` which imports the API, a new `NOTES.md`, and a deleted `legacy.js`. It is too big to review in one pull request. I want the data model, the API, and the page reviewed as separate units. Split that branch into a stack using `{default_branch}` as the trunk, preserving every change including the deletion. Do not push or open pull requests. Work autonomously.
assertions: The stack has at least three dependent layers.
The top of the stack reproduces the original commit exactly.
The legacy.js deletion is preserved.
Dependency order is respected.
No layer is empty and the worktree is clean.

name: split-open-pr
prompt_template: Pull request #{source_pr} (branch `{branch_prefix}/big`, base `{default_branch}`) is too large to review. Under `eval/{run_id}/` it adds `model.js`, `api.js` which imports the model, `page.js` which imports the API, and `NOTES.md`, and deletes `legacy.js`. I want the data model, the API, and the page reviewed as separate units. Split it into a stack of dependent branches, preserving every change including the deletion, and make sure the original pull request is either reused as the top layer or closed. Work autonomously.
assertions: The stack has at least three dependent layers.
The top of the stack reproduces the original PR head exactly.
Dependency order is respected.
The original pull request is reused as the top layer or closed.
No layer is empty and the worktree is clean.

name: continue-stack
prompt_template: Continue the current stack with a new top layer named `{branch_prefix}/audit`. Add `eval/{run_id}/audit.js`, which imports `page.js` and exports `auditUser(user)`. Commit the new layer, remain on it, and do not push. Work autonomously.
assertions: The stack gains a fourth top layer with the requested name.
The new layer contains audit.js and depends on the previous top layer.
The existing three layers remain unchanged.
The run finishes on the new top layer with a clean worktree.

name: link-stack
prompt_template: Branches `{branch_prefix}/base` and `{branch_prefix}/top` already form a dependency chain but are not tracked by gh-stack. Link them into a GitHub Stack with `{default_branch}` as the ultimate base, open both pull requests ready for review, and do not create local gh-stack tracking. Work autonomously.
assertions: Both pull requests are open and ready for review.
The top PR targets the base branch.
Both PRs belong to one GitHub Stack.
No local gh-stack tracking file is created.
